codeReview.summary: Clean, well-scoped implementation. The `parseVerdictFromText` and `parseValidatorVerdict` functions correctly accept an optional `strictness` parameter defaulting to 'strict'. The `runValidator` function reads `validatorStrictness` from config (defaulting to 'strict') and applies it consistently to timeout/abort and missing-verdict paths. All 5 expectedBehavior items are covered by the 18 new tests. Existing tests were properly updated to opt into 'lenient' mode where they relied on old pass-on-error behavior. The diff is minimal and focused — only `validate-worker.ts` has functional changes; all other file changes are test updates or formatting-only (Biome auto-format). The `validatorStrictness` field was already present in both `MissionConfig` interface and `MissionConfigSchema` (from a precondition/prior feature), so no schema changes were needed in this commit.

issues.description: The lenient-mode fallback message for timeout/abort says 'Validator timed out or was aborted — assuming pass.' regardless of which actually happened. In strict mode, the message correctly distinguishes the two cases via a ternary. This inconsistency is cosmetic and does not affect behavior, but could be confusing in logs.

sharedStateObservations.observation: When existing tests relied on the old pass-on-error validator behavior, the worker correctly added `saveConfig(basePath, { validatorStrictness: 'lenient' })` calls to preserve their semantics. This pattern (explicitly opting into lenient for backward-compat) is now a testing convention but is not documented in AGENTS.md. Future workers modifying spawn-worker or integration tests that trigger validation should know to either set validatorStrictness in test config or account for the strict default.

summary: The stricter-validator feature is correctly implemented. The core logic in validate-worker.ts adds a strictness parameter to parseVerdictFromText and parseValidatorVerdict (defaulting to 'strict'), and runValidator reads validatorStrictness from config. Strict mode rejects on timeout, abort, and missing verdict; lenient mode preserves the old pass behavior. 18 new tests comprehensively cover all scenarios including default-is-strict. Existing tests properly updated to use lenient mode where needed. The only minor observation is an inconsistent feedback message in the lenient timeout/abort path (cosmetic). All VAL-VALIDATOR assertions (001-003, 005-006) are fulfilled.
